messages:
Luca: quick FYI — during the AWQ-int8 bring-up on prod-like cluster we started seeing intermittent p95 spikes (~300ms -> ~1.2s) that line up with prefix KV cache warmup + continuous batching coalescer kicking in. seems like warmup thrash when a cold key hits while a batch is assembling. :eyes:
Maya: can you paste the grafana panel and the time-range? curious if it's tied to specific sequence lengths or request patterns.
Luca: panel: https://grafana.redwood/d/abcd/kv-batch?from=now-30m to=now
Luca: repro window 2026-03-18T15:02:00Z - 15:18:00Z
Dennis: saw that pattern before with small-prefix workloads — batcher waits up to 10ms to coalesce, if warmup (kv load + quantized kernel init) hits in the middle it blocks the whole batch. attached a short log excerpt.
Dennis: ```
[15:03:11.123] batcher: assembling batch size=6 wait=10ms
[15:03:11.128] kvcache: miss key=usr:123:ctx -> async warmup start
[15:03:11.132] kernel: awq int8 load model shard 12 init_gemm
[15:03:11.226] batcher: execute batch -> single request latency jump
```
Sophia: important: do we see any eval/regression on quality from AWQ-int8? latency spikes are bad but if quality regressed we treat differently.
Luca: quick check on eval harness (prompt-suite v1.3) — EM/ROUGE stable within noise vs fp8 baseline. quality unchanged. only perf jitter. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Ana: two quick mitigations: 1) cold-kv warmup offload (background preloader with lower priority) 2) reduce batcher max-wait for small-prefix traffic so we fall back to single-request path instead of blocking.
Maya: try 1) and 2) in a canary? also add histograms for kernel init time and kv warmup time.
Luca: scheduled canary on dedicated pool (10% traffic) now. deploy-bot: deploy started for canary pool "kv-warmup-experiments" (rev: awq-int8-patch-20260318).
deploy-bot: status: rolling -> 5/10 nodes updated
Luca: canary results after 30m: p50 little change, p95 improved from 1.2s->420ms, p99 still occasional ~900ms. kernel init accounted for ~70% of warmup cost.
Dennis: interesting — kernel init is non-idempotent cost when quantized kernels lazily JIT/cache cpu/gpu kernels. we should persist kernel warm cache at node boot for awq-int8 variant.
Sophia: does persisting kernel cache change memory footprint or startup time? might affect Dedicated nodes.
Ana: small bump in resident mem during boot, negligible (<150MB) for our 80GB GPU nodes. tradeoff seems worth it to stabilize latency.
Maya: next steps: a) persist quant-kernel cache on boot for awq-int8, b) implement low-priority background KV preloader for long-tail prefixes, c) add metric: warmup_block_time to trace spans. canary -> prod if 24h stable.
Luca: I'll open a small RFC with config knobs + perf plots and tag eng-ml/eng-runtime. also adding a quick local repro script.
Luca: repro snippet: ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://canary-api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"input":"prefix user_${RANDOM}: short prompt"}' >/dev/null &
done
wait
```
Dennis: thanks — let's keep the kernel init metric to correlate with batch latencies. if anyone wants the raw traces I uploaded them to s3://redwood-perf/kv_warmup/1965432100.tar.gz
Sophia: awesome. please include the eval harness run id in the RFC so product/stability can sign off.
Ana: tagging ops for runtime boot config changes. :thumbsup: 
Luca: tagging done, will follow up with RFC link and canary dashboard after full collection.
